trust_decision.summary: Whether the JupyterLab ServerUrl returned by the (codespace-controlled) gRPC server is trusted enough to hand to the local OS browser/URL-handler launcher; at the pinned commit it is accepted unchecked in StartJupyterServer and opened in Jupyter.

landing_point.why: The summary names `gh codespace jupyter`; its command file shows the server URL going straight into a.browser.Browse.

fix_sites.module_kind: internal RPC client wrapper (lower-level than the command)

fix_sites.entry_point: same; new helper isJupyterServerURLValid added in internal/codespaces/rpc/invoker.go
fix_sites.module_kind: validation helper in the same file

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: internal/codespaces/rpc/invoker.go:168-187 (fix lives in the RPC invoker, one package below the landing point pkg/cmd/codespace/jupyter.go:92); it is the only Invoker implementation (internal/codespaces/rpc/invoker.go:44)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Weak: a solver validating at jupyter.go:92 instead of in the invoker is still fully correct, as jupyter.go:64 is the only caller of StartJupyterServer; there is no second route to dismiss.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate Jupyter URLs must keep opening: http/https to localhost, 127.0.0.1 and [::1], keeping the auth token in the query string (and the port rewrite at jupyter.go:91). An over-broad fix that rejects query strings, https, IPv6 loopback or 'localhost' would break the command.

O6_input_shapes: allowed: localhost (case-insensitive), IPv4 loopback, IPv6 loopback

O7_producer.where: Value comes straight from the gRPC response field (internal/codespaces/rpc/jupyter/jupyter_server_host_service.v1.pb.go:69); no intermediate producer

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Post-check rewrite: strings.Replace swaps the first occurrence of the server-reported port digits for the local port, and the reported Port (invoker.go:182) is never tied to the URL's own port, so the URL that gets opened can differ from the one validated (how-type 'rename after the check').
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Present in the real code: the maintainers added the check inside the invoker but left the string-based port substitution in the command, and it is never re-validated.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A planted codespace-supplied field from StartSSHServerWithOptions (for example a hostname or extra option) that reaches the ssh exec at pkg/cmd/codespace/ssh.go:495 without a check like isUsernameValid.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same file already validates the server-returned username (invoker.go:245); a new server-returned field could plausibly be added without that check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A planted variant where `gh codespace code` builds its browse URL from a codespace-side RPC value instead of the API WebURL.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same Browse sink and the same command family; a where-type extra only.

O9_family: CWE-829 untrusted remote-supplied URL passed to the local OS URL/scheme-handler launcher (inclusion of functionality from an untrusted control sphere)

O10_build.project_tests: internal/codespaces/rpc/invoker_test.go (TestStartJupyterServerSuccess/Failure with an in-process gRPC mock); pkg/cmd/codespace tests use browser.Stub

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Check only that the URL starts with http:// or https:// at jupyter.go:92, without checking for a loopback host or re-checking after the port rewrite.

out_of_scope_notes: pkg/cmd/codespace/code.go:44 opens codespace.WebURL, but that comes from the GitHub API, not from the codespace, so it is a different trust source.
unverified: Repo size in MB was not measured.

Whether the jupyter.go:91 port substitution can actually turn a validated loopback URL into a non-loopback or otherwise harmful one in real browsers was not tested; the sibling is described from reading the code only.
Whether the single_site flag holds strictly: the fix touches one function plus a new helper in one file, and no O8 route was found.
